eMqhekezweni Rape Extortion

By: Sipha Kema | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A tranquil village once knoA once tranquil village in the Eastern Cape is under siege as unknown masked gang of criminals torment the women of eMqhekezweni extorting money with the threat of sexual as

Unique Selling Point:
In the heart of the Eastern Cape province lies a small village, eMqhekezweni, just outside Mthatha. This village, once known for its tranquility and close-knit community and the second home of the iconic late former President Nelson Mandela, has been plagued by a sinister threat that has left its women living in constant fear and despair. A balaclava-clad gang has emerged, running a ruthless extortion racket that forces women to pay a protection fee to avoid the threat of rape. With limited police visibility due to resource constraints and the Bityi police station – which services 60 other villages, located 25kms from the village, the women of eMqhekezweni are left feeling hopeless and vulnerable.

Summary:
Within eMqhekezweni, the devious group preys on women of all ages. This balaclava-clad gang operates with audacity, instilling fear in the hearts of the villagers. Their method is simple yet effective - they demand a protection fee from every woman, exploiting their vulnerability and capitalizing on their fear of sexual assault. For those unable to pay, the consequences are dire, as they become targets for the gang's violent acts. The minimum fee charged by the gang is R400, money most homes cannot afford to part with. These criminals target women headed households, girls’ high school private boarding facilities and households headed by elderly defenceless men.


The presence of this gang has cast a dark shadow over the lives of the women in eMqhekezweni. Fear has become a constant companion, affecting their daily routines and lives. The women, young and old alike, are haunted by the looming threat of violence. This fear has not only shattered their sense of security but has also limited their ability to live their lives to the fullest. A few of the Jongintaba Senior Secondary School girl learners have dropped out of School and have gone back home because of this menacing tactics. The weight of hopelessness looms heavy, leaving these women and young girls trapped in a cycle of despair.



Further information:
While the women of eMqhekezweni suffer, the local police force faces its own set of challenges. Limited resources have severely impacted their ability to combat this growing issue effectively. With insufficient manpower and equipment, police visibility in the village is scarce. The Bityi police station, responsible for eMqhekezweni's security, is situated 2k5kms from eMqhekezweni. This lone police station is servicing 62 clusters of villages it challenging for law enforcement to respond promptly to reported incidents with one police vehicle as the furthest village is over an hour’s drive. This lack of resources and proximity has further worsen the vulnerability of the village's women.

The visit by the Eastern Cape government, led by Premier Oscar Mabuyane and Police Minister Bheki Cele, to the eMqhekezweni village was intended to address the alarming rise in attacks on women. However, despite promising initiatives such as the construction of a satellite police station, extra police vehicles and increased night patrols, none of these commitments have been fulfilled.
The visit will have taken place a month ago when we shoot in Mqhekezweni.

Press Release:


Rape Extortion Racket  

In eMqhekezweni, a small village in the Eastern Cape, women are on edge. This village, once known for its tranquillity and close-knit community and the second home of former President Nelson Mandela, has been plagued by a sinister threat that has left women living in constant fear and despair. A balaclava-clad gang has emerged, running a ruthless extortion racket. At dusk, men on horseback terrorise villagers, demanding that young girls and women of all ages, pay a protection fee or get raped by their tormentors. Most of the people in this village are poor and can’t afford to pay, but help from the police is kilometres away and, in this area, visible policing is a myth.  

Producer: Sipha Kema | Presenter: Govan Whittles

The satellite police station, more officers on the ground and the much needed extra vehicles all depend on whether Bityi Police Station meets the requirements for an upgrade.

Later on, we learnt that the most fruitful investigation of the balaclava gang, which led to 3 arrests, was conducted by the community and NOT the police. It happened after the last break-in at Nokhaya's boarding facility.

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 10 December 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Rape Extortion Racket In eMqhekezweni, a small village in the Eastern Cape, women are on edge. This village, once known for its tranquillity and close-knit community and the second home of former President Nelson Mandela, has been plagued by a sinister threat that has left women living in constant fear and despair. A balaclava-clad gang has emerged, running a ruthless extortion racket. At dusk, men on horseback terrorise villagers, demanding that young girls and women of all ages, pay a protection fee or get raped by their tormentors. Most of the people in this village are poor and can’t afford to pay, but help from the police is kilometres away and, in this area, visible policing is a myth. metadata.Unique Selling Point: In the heart of the Eastern Cape province lies a small village, eMqhekezweni, just outside Mthatha. This village, once known for its tranquility and close-knit community and the second home of the iconic late former President Nelson Mandela, has been plagued by a sinister threat that has left its women living in constant fear and despair. A balaclava-clad gang has emerged, running a ruthless extortion racket that forces women to pay a protection fee to avoid the threat of rape. With limited police visibility due to resource constraints and the Bityi police station – which services 60 other villages, located 25kms from the village, the women of eMqhekezweni are left feeling hopeless and vulnerable.
metadata.Summary: Within eMqhekezweni, the devious group preys on women of all ages. This balaclava-clad gang operates with audacity, instilling fear in the hearts of the villagers. Their method is simple yet effective - they demand a protection fee from every woman, exploiting their vulnerability and capitalizing on their fear of sexual assault. For those unable to pay, the consequences are dire, as they become targets for the gang's violent acts. The minimum fee charged by the gang is R400, money most homes cannot afford to part with. These criminals target women headed households, girls’ high school private boarding facilities and households headed by elderly defenceless men. The presence of this gang has cast a dark shadow over the lives of the women in eMqhekezweni. Fear has become a constant companion, affecting their daily routines and lives. The women, young and old alike, are haunted by the looming threat of violence. This fear has not only shattered their sense of security but has also limited their ability to live their lives to the fullest. A few of the Jongintaba Senior Secondary School girl learners have dropped out of School and have gone back home because of this menacing tactics. The weight of hopelessness looms heavy, leaving these women and young girls trapped in a cycle of despair.
metadata.Further information: While the women of eMqhekezweni suffer, the local police force faces its own set of challenges. Limited resources have severely impacted their ability to combat this growing issue effectively. With insufficient manpower and equipment, police visibility in the village is scarce. The Bityi police station, responsible for eMqhekezweni's security, is situated 2k5kms from eMqhekezweni. This lone police station is servicing 62 clusters of villages it challenging for law enforcement to respond promptly to reported incidents with one police vehicle as the furthest village is over an hour’s drive. This lack of resources and proximity has further worsen the vulnerability of the village's women. The visit by the Eastern Cape government, led by Premier Oscar Mabuyane and Police Minister Bheki Cele, to the eMqhekezweni village was intended to address the alarming rise in attacks on women. However, despite promising initiatives such as the construction of a satellite police station, extra police vehicles and increased night patrols, none of these commitments have been fulfilled. The visit will have taken place a month ago when we shoot in Mqhekezweni.
